So, are you ready to climb the pyramid and unlock its secrets? Let's get started!

sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Pyramid Solitaire Classic is a game about removing all cards from a pyramid-shaped layout. The pyramid is made up of 28 cards, arranged in a triangular shape. The cards in the pyramid are face-up, and you can see the values of each card. The game also has a draw pile, which contains the remaining cards in the deck.

The objective of the game is to remove all cards from the pyramid by combining two cards to a total value of 13. Sounds simple, right? But here's the twist - each card has a unique value. The numerical cards are worth their face value, while the A, J, Q, and K cards have the following values: A=1, J=11, Q=12, and K=13. The King is the only card that can be removed as a single card, as it's worth 13 points.

To remove a card from the pyramid, you need to combine two cards that add up to 13. You can use the cards in the draw pile to get a new face-up card. If you have a card that's not part of a valid combination, you can use it to add to your draw pile or discard it.

One of the key features of Pyramid Solitaire Classic is its undo function. If you make a mistake or want to try a different approach, you can undo your last move and start again. This makes the game much more accessible and fun to play.

Overall, the core gameplay mechanics of Pyramid Solitaire Classic are easy to learn but challenging to master. With its unique card values and removal mechanism, the game offers a refreshing twist on the classic solitaire game.
